title: Peak readiness surge slate and demo rotations - Q3 readiness draft
content:
Context and intent

This is a working slate for the company-wide Q3 readiness window we call "Peak Readiness Surge" (target window: Aug 24 – Sep 18). Purpose: align exec asks, surface dependencies, and create a low-friction demo rotation cadence for all-hands rehearsal and customer-facing show-and-tell. This doc mixes draft OKRs, a proposed run-of-show for the all-hands rehearsal day, and a lightweight escalation/runbook outline.

High-level objectives for the window (why we care)
- Prevent last-minute performance or capacity regressions ahead of expected customer usage bumps in late Sep.
- Align teams on 3 cross-company priorities to ship with confidence: (A) Dedicated capacity SLA tightening, (B) Hosted API cost optimizations, (C) Rollout safety for private deployments v1.2.
- Run a repeatable demo rotation so every product/solutions PM can rehearse short customer narratives and a fallback story.

Draft OKRs (company-level, for alignment during Surge)
O1: Tighten reliability and capacity margins to meet new SLAs
KR1.1: Reduce 95th percentile tail latency for hosted text-gen by 15% in target 1–4s buckets (measured on synthetic traffic + 2 customer traces).
KR1.2: Guarantee 99.9% availability for Dedicated pools with pre-provisioned burst capacity rules in 90%+ of test scenarios.
KR1.3: Complete end-to-end failure-mode drills for Private deployments in 3 regulated customer environments.

O2: Improve unit economics without degrading output quality
KR2.1: Deploy automated prefix caching for top-10 high-volume routes; +10% cache hit rate baseline.
KR2.2: Ship conservative quantization profile for two high-usage model families and show <3% quality delta on curated evals.
KR2.3: Reduce per-token cost for hosted API by 8% via batching and routing changes (A/B test).

O3: Strengthen customer-facing readiness and narrative
KR3.1: Complete demo rotation with 18 teams (3-min slot + 2-min Q&A) and a documented fallback script for each demo.
KR3.2: Produce a customer-ready one-pager for Dedicated/Private differentiators and availability windows.
KR3.3: Run two external pilot rehearsals with top-5 GL customers and collect satisfaction >= 80%.

Scope and out-of-scope
- In-scope: SRE, Serving Runtime, Product (Hosted, Dedicated, Private), Solutions Engineering, Console/Observability tweaks needed for the demo experience.
- Out-of-scope: Model research experiments that require training changes; long-term cost projects not deliverable within the window.

Proposed timeline (milestones)
- Jul 20–Jul 31: Readiness intake and dependency map (complete).  Owners must file the short intake doc (link in linked_artifacts).
- Aug 1–Aug 14: Engineering stabilization sprint (perf work, autoscale rules, KV caching rollout).
- Aug 15–Aug 21: Demo content freeze + dry-runs per team.
- Aug 24–Sep 4: Staged chaos & failure-mode drills + runbook iteration.
- Sep 7–Sep 11: Executive rehearsal and SLT sign-off.
- Sep 14–Sep 18: Customer pilot dry-run and soft launch of comms.

All-hands rehearsal: run-of-show (single day suggested)
- 09:00–09:15: Context + objectives (CEO/COO) — what success looks like for the Surge.
- 09:15–09:40: Reliability snapshot (SRE) — current risk map, mitigation actions, short ask list.
- 09:40–10:10: Product quick-fire (3x 10-min blocks) — Hosted API, Dedicated, Private (each: one slide + 3-min demo + fallback plan).
- 10:10–10:25: Breakouts sign-up (teams pick demo slots for external rehearsals).
- 10:25–11:45: Demo rotations — 18 teams in slots (3-min demo, 2-min questions). Keep slides to 1–2 each; demos must have a fallback.
- 11:45–12:00: Rapid decisions & next steps (Ops lead recaps).

Demo rotation guidelines (must-haves)
- Duration: 3 minutes demo, 2 minutes Q&A (strict timing).
- Must include: short problem framing, expected customer impact, fallback policy if service-level is degraded.
- Tech checklist (to verify before slot): demo runbook in repo, metrics dashboard link, local mock data sanitized, fallback response tested.
- Each demo owner to provide a 1-paragraph fallback script watchers can read if live demo fails.

Runbook / escalation matrix (lightweight)
- Tier 0: Pre-flight failures (demo environment missing dashboards, keys) — Solutions Eng lead handles; target resolution < 2 hours.
- Tier 1: Performance regressions on staging (<3x preconfigured thresholds) — SRE pager + dev on-call; target mitigation < 30 minutes using routing fallback.
- Tier 2: Degradation in production impacting customers — Exec on-call escalation; initiate customer comms template + automatic traffic shift to fallback model/region.

Owners and immediate asks (short list)
- SRE: final verification of autoscale/burst policy for Dedicated pools (owner: Evan Roberts). Ask: complete test harness by Aug 7.
- Serving Runtime: KV cache rollout and latency regressions (owner: Diego Alvarez). Ask: perf benchmark matrix by Aug 10.
- Product Hosted API: batching + routing A/B config (owner: Priya Iyer). Ask: A/B flag and monitoring plan by Aug 9.
- Solutions Eng: demo orchestration, customer pilot coordination (owner: Ruth Osei). Ask: confirm pilot customers and availability by Jul 28.
- Communications: customer one-pager and internal quick FAQ (owner: Maya Chen). Ask: first draft by Aug 1.

Risks and mitigations (notes-to-self style)
- Risk: Late-breaking kernel regressions from upstream runtime change.  Mitigation: freeze kernel changes for the window + require SRE signoff.
- Risk: Demos over-run and crowd out rehearsal time. Mitigation: strict timer and pre-uploaded slide limit.
- Risk: Pilot customers not available. Mitigation: identify 2 backups per pilot.

Comms plan (internal + external)
- Internal: Daily 9:30 stand for control-room participants during Aug 24–Sep 4; Slack channel #peak-surge for status. Weekly exec summary Thursdays.
- External: Customer one-pager + targeted emails after SLT sign-off (Sep 8). Template in linked_artifacts.

Open questions / decision log (please update)
- Q: Do we allow kernel-level perf changes during the stabilization sprint (Aug 1–Aug 14)?  Proposed: no, unless emergency; require signoff.
- Q: Final list of demo owners — Ruth to publish by Jul 28.
- Q: Which metric thresholds trigger automatic fallback routing?  SRE to propose by Aug 4.

Next steps (owners + immediate actions)
- Maya: finalize comms one-pager draft by Aug 1.
- Evan: publish autoscale test harness and schedule demo slice test Aug 5–7.
- Diego: deliver perf matrix and verify cache behavior on the top-10 routes by Aug 10.
- Priya: enable A/B flags in staging and prepare quality checks by Aug 8.
- Ruth: confirm demo roster and mock customer scripts by Jul 28.

Notes / informal fragments (working doc)
- Keep demo stories short — think customer problem -> Redwood solution -> fallback.
- Consider a short pre-recorded video for any demo touching a fragile third-party integration.
- If pilot customers ask for deeper SLA guarantees, feeders to sales/solutions need a fast path to procurement.

If you’re an owner and don’t see your work captured: add a one-line entry in the intake doc referenced in linked_artifacts. This is intentionally light — the goal is alignment and a set of pragmatic, testable commitments for the next 6 weeks.

-- end --
